## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
One policy breach needs fixing: the new `--exclude` flag ignores the `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE` environment variable that the project's CLI-flag rule requires for new flags, so CI cannot set exclusions through the environment.

## Changes
The pull request adds a repeatable `--exclude GLOB` flag that skips files whose basename matches any pattern. Skipped files are logged at info level. It also documents the flag in `docs/flags.md`, adds tests for parsing, collection and archive output, and adds a one-line text fixture.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- cli/main.py:17 — correctness — Read the --exclude default from ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE — If CI sets `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE=*.log` and runs `archive src`, `.log` files are still archived, because `--exclude` uses `default=[]` and never reads the environment. This breaks the rule at `.claude/skills/cli-flags/SKILL.md:11`: "Every command-line flag added under `cli/` from now on must also take its default from an `ARCHIVE_<NAME>` environment variable". — CI pipelines that set options through the environment cannot exclude files, and their archives silently include unwanted files. — Fix: Parse `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE` into a list using a delimiter you document, and pass a fresh copy as `default`, because `action="append"` adds CLI values to the default list and modifies it in place; extend `test_exclude_defaults_to_nothing` with an environment case.
